Jane — attaching the mutual action plan (v2) and a short run plan for our performance evaluation. The goal: produce a clear pass/fail for your SLOs (95th latency < 400ms at target QPS, sustained throughput target 120 req/s, TTFT median < 180ms) and to validate burst behavior up to 4x baseline.

High-level schedule (in MAP):
- Nov 11-13: Test harness and environment validation (baseline, environment parity checks)
- Nov 14-16: Steady-state runs at 0.5x/1x/1.5x/2x load to establish queueing curves
- Nov 17: Burst runs (step to 4x for 60s, repeated 3x) to validate transient throttling and fallback routing
- Nov 18-19: Repeat runs with KV-caching ON/OFF and batching profiles from Red-Opt 1/2
- Nov 19: Aggregate results, produce Gatling summary + CSVs

Key pass/fail criteria we agreed in the MAP:
- 95th latency <= 400ms at target QPS (120 req/s)
- TTFT median <= 180ms under steady-state 1x
- No >1% request errors (5xx or timeouts) in steady-state
- System gracefully degrades under burst (controlled queueing, no hard drops)

Attachments: MAP-v2.xlsx (action items + owners), test-harness-checklist.txt (inline in MAP), sample-gatling-config.conf snippet

Next steps: please confirm the action owners in the attached MAP and that Nov 14-19 is still good from your side. If you want us to run additional model variant tests (quantized vs float), call that out on the MAP sheet.

Jane — ran the full suite yesterday and attached the Gatling HTML summary + raw CSVs. High-level readout below (see attachments for per-run details).

Summary (all tests run against v3.2.1-quant on prod-like dedicated pool):
- Steady-state 1x (120 req/s): median TTFT = 142ms, 95th latency = 368ms, error rate = 0.3%
- Steady-state 2x (240 req/s): median TTFT = 266ms, 95th latency = 712ms, error rate = 1.7% (queueing increases beyond 180s window)
- Burst 3x (360 req/s, 30s sustained): transient queueing observed, p95 spiked to 1.2s, 5xx increased to 2.4% during spike, fallback routing engaged for 12% of requests (successful but higher latency)
- Burst 4x (480 req/s, 60s spikes): system applied backpressure; throttling thresholds kicked in, many requests delayed; p95 reached 1.9s, error rate peaked at 5.6% (exceeds MAP target)

Notes and recommendations:
1) For Acme's production SLO (95th <= 400ms at 120 req/s) the platform passes on the steady-state 1x profile.
2) TTFT cold-starts (measured separately): median cold TTFT = 310ms — aligns with your expectation. We recommend pre-warming critical pods for peak windows.
3) Burst tolerance: current default throttling policy is too aggressive at sustained >3x spikes. Two options: a) tune rate-limit windows (increase burst window to allow short sustained spikes) or b) enable optional queue-backing with larger worker pool and graceful shedding. Option (a) reduces transient failures but increases tail latency; (b) reduces tail latency but requires reserved headroom.
4) Batching: Red-Opt1 batching improved throughput by ~18% and reduced p95 under 2x by ~120ms. Recommend Red-Opt1 for your traffic profile.

Attachments: gatling-summary-20261119.html, throughput-ttft-csv-20261119.csv

Action items captured back into MAP-v2.xlsx:
- Redwood: propose rate-limit tune (option a) and run follow-up 3x-burst test — owner: Vivek — ETA: Nov 22
- Acme: confirm whether preferred approach is (a) or (b) — owner: Jane — ETA: Nov 21
- Redwood: prepare a procurement-friendly one-pager on reserved headroom cost for option (b) — owner: Neha — ETA: Nov 24

Let me know if you want a quick call tomorrow to walk the Gatling plots.

Best,
Vivek
